paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's people don't just hear His words, they say "Amen" to them out loud. Moses tells Israel, "Be silent, O Israel, and listen! This day you have become the people of the LORD your God." (Deuteronomy 27:9) Notice the order. They are God's people first, and then comes the obedience, so the obeying grows out of belonging.

Look at what the curses actually cover, baker. Some are out in the open, like withholding justice from the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow (Deuteronomy 27:19), while others are done in secret, like the idol set up in secret (Deuteronomy 27:15) and the neighbor struck down in secret (Deuteronomy 27:24). The words go on those plastered stones and get written distinctly, so nobody can say the instructions were blurry. I stamped blurry for years, and God does not do blurry.

And then the last one gets everybody, because it says, "Cursed is he who does not put the words of this law into practice." (Deuteronomy 27:26) Hearing isn't the finish line, friend, doing is. So when you open the Word this week, ask what you're going to do about it, not just what you read, and say your own quiet Amen. The sermon isn't over yet, so keep that oven warm.
